answer_or_rule_with_label: Rule (INFERENCE): the replication arms (ethosuximide and lithium) use PTZ given i.p. in one injection, because the replication condition is Cheng 2020 (held full text, Methods paragraph on seizure induction and Fig. 7 legend; the brief itself names no assay except as that condition, V2 line 29). All other arms may use the laboratory's own published PTZ protocol provided the SAME stimulus is given to every genotype and arm of a session and gives wild-type pups a non-floor response (V2 lines 25 and 29). A different provoked-seizure assay is a different experiment, not a variant.
what_changes_it: The laboratory does not run PTZ or cannot meet the Cheng condition
question_for_the_laboratory_or_operator: Laboratory: do you run PTZ-provoked seizures in pups as a published standard assay, by which route and schedule, and could you give the single i.p. injection used in Cheng 2020 for the replication arms?

answer_or_rule_with_label: Dose and route of PTZ used by Cheng 2020 are printed in the held full text (Methods paragraph on seizure induction; repeated in the Fig. 7b legend). It is one single PTZ dose given to all three genotypes (the Results call it 'a low dose of PTZ'). The injected volume is NOT printed (only 'dissolved in 0.9% sodium chloride'). The brief deliberately does not copy numbers (no-dose perimeter); the text should point to the Cheng 2020 Methods instead of copying them.
locator: Cheng 2020 Methods and Fig. 7 legend; V2 line 33
what_changes_it: The laboratory's own standard volume or schedule
question_for_the_laboratory_or_operator: Laboratory: what volume per body weight and what vehicle do you use for the PTZ injection?

answer_or_rule_with_label: (1) Held fact: Cheng 2020 printed the ethosuximide dose, route (i.p.), a single injection and the interval before PTZ (held Methods). (2) Rule (INFERENCE, same logic the brief states for lithium at V2 line 33): the Cheng regimen is the replication condition and the main ethosuximide contrast; the brief's dose check then adds ONE further exposure per agent per age (V2 line 33 'two exposures per agent'); that second value is not derivable from held numbers.
what_changes_it: The laboratory's own pup exposure data or a published pup exposure
question_for_the_laboratory_or_operator: Laboratory: what second exposure of ethosuximide would you add per age, and do you have a published or measured pup exposure for either?

answer_or_rule_with_label: Rule (INFERENCE, double-dummy): every pup in a session gets the same number, volume and timing of injections, with the agent present or replaced by saline. The two Cheng regimens differ in schedule (lithium three injections within one hour; ethosuximide one injection 45 minutes before PTZ, both in saline, held Methods), so a single vehicle group is valid only if it receives the SAME schedule as the arm with the most injections and every other arm receives saline for the injections it does not need. Without that, V2 line 25 ('one vehicle group per genotype shared by all arms') cannot hold for arms with different schedules.
what_changes_it: A laboratory that cannot give saline injections to arms for blinding or welfare reasons (then one vehicle group per schedule)
question_for_the_laboratory_or_operator: Laboratory: can every pup receive the same number of injections (drug or saline) so that one vehicle group serves all arms?

answer_or_rule_with_label: Held: the modified Racine scale of Cheng 2020 is printed in the Methods: stage 0 no response; 1 behavioural arrest then vibrissae twitching; 2 head nodding; 3 unilateral forelimb clonus with a myoclonic jerk; 4 bilateral forelimb clonus with rearing; 5 generalised tonic-clonic seizure with loss of righting; 6 dead. The brief's definitions (2.6) are consistent with it; stage 6 IS death.
question_for_the_laboratory_or_operator: Closed by text; the V2 text can cite the Cheng scale by locator instead of paraphrasing.

answer_or_rule_with_label: Inconsistency in the brief: the pilot row (V2 line 41) lists vehicle pups only, while its stop rule refers to the panel agent. Rule (INFERENCE): the pilot includes the flat-profile panel agent in wild-type pups at each candidate age (otherwise the stop rule cannot fire) and uses the ages the brief already names: P11 and P14 (V2 line 26, 'straddling P11 and P14'); knockout feasible ages are bounded above by the earlier of the two held death statements (about day 17 in the comparator's panel, V2 line 82; about 4 weeks in Cheng 2020). A third later age depends on the laboratory's colony survival.
locator: V2 lines 26, 41, 82; Cheng 2020 Introduction and Results
question_for_the_laboratory_or_operator: Laboratory: up to what postnatal day can knockout pups in your colony be tested with a provoked-seizure assay without losing more than a stated fraction before the test?

answer_or_rule_with_label: Rule (INFERENCE): 'stage-matched wild-type response' = under ONE stimulus given identically to both genotypes (V2 line 25, same session, same age), wild-type vehicle pups are not at the floor by the Q68 rule and the wild-type and knockout vehicle S distributions overlap at the stage level. The stimulus may NOT differ by genotype for a comparison that feeds the interaction ratio (two stimuli would confound the ratio). If no single stimulus meets both conditions, that is the pilot's stop rule firing.

answer_or_rule_with_label: Rule (INFERENCE): the same stimulus at every age of the wild-type series (V2 line 27 'same stimulus and scale'), because the series is meant to show whether a wild-type non-response is age; the pilot therefore must include wild-type vehicle pups at the older ages too (cheap: no knockout needed) so that the stimulus is fixed knowing the older-age response. Re-fixing the stimulus per age would turn age and stimulus into one variable; if an older age is at the floor or ceiling the series records it and a second stimulus level is an extra cell, not a replacement.
what_changes_it: The laboratory's own view that the stimulus must scale with age
question_for_the_laboratory_or_operator: Laboratory: does the same stimulus remain tolerable and informative at the older ages of the series?

answer_or_rule_with_label: Rule (INFERENCE): decide on pilot VEHICLE animals only, before any treated-arm data, in a dated note signed before stage 2. Switch the primary outcome from S to generalised-seizure incidence if the pilot SD of log S in the knockout vehicle group gives n per arm for ratio 0.7 above the number of knockouts the laboratory can supply: n per arm = 2 x 7.85 x sigma^2 / 0.1272 (two-sided 0.05, power 0.80). At the brief's binary example (fall from 50 to 10 percent) about 20 per arm (V2 line 46). Who decides: ADV with the laboratory, in writing, before stage 2; the brief already says S is primary unless the pilot finds a far less variable summary (V2 line 11).
question_for_the_laboratory_or_operator: Laboratory: how many knockout pups per genotype-by-arm cell can you realistically supply in one session and in total?

answer_or_rule_with_label: Restated from the brief's own arithmetic (V2 line 47), no new value: 27 cells = wild-type age series 3 ages x [vehicle; ethosuximide at 2 exposures; flat-profile panel agent at 2 exposures; rising-profile panel agent at 2 exposures] = 3 x 7 = 21 cells, plus knockout and heterozygote at the assay age x [vehicle; ethosuximide at 2 exposures] = 2 x 3 = 6 cells. NOT in the 27: lithium and lithium-alone, the second GSK-3 inhibitor, the general comparator, the T-type blocker (optional or stage 3), the falling-profile agent, any older-age knockout or heterozygote cell. Wild-type cells at the assay age sit inside the 21.
question_for_the_laboratory_or_operator: Closed by text; a cell table can be generated from this sentence.

answer_or_rule_with_label: Mapping of the figures in the briefs (INFERENCE where noted, from the held addendum inputs): 11 and 31 and 79 per arm = simple effect at sigma_log 0.3, 0.5, 0.8; 22 = interaction at sigma 0.3 with equal sigma (twice 11); 44 = the superseded 'four times' error; 50 = an illustration; 36 to 109 = simple effect in knockouts at sigma 0.54 to 0.94 (addendum); 180 to 320 = interaction per cell with wild-type sigma 1.07 to 1.30 (see C06). For the first run (pilot) the brief already states 6 to 8 per cell (V2 line 41). For stage 2, rule: n per arm = n_simple(sigma-hat from the pilot) with sigma-hat inflated by one relative standard error of an SD (1/sqrt(2(n-1)): 0.29 at n = 7), which at the addendum's range moves 36 to 60 and 109 to 181 per arm.

answer_or_rule_with_label: Held statements disagree: V2 line 31 says one shared vehicle group per genotype of about twice a test arm (square-root rule); V2 line 47 totals 27 cells at 11 per cell = 297 animals, i.e. vehicle cells at 11 (not doubled). Computed (INFERENCE, square-root rule n_vehicle = n x sqrt(k) per age and genotype): at 11 per arm the total is about 354, not about 300 (WT per age 6 arms: 66 + 26.9 = 92.9; knockout and heterozygote 2 arms each: 22 + 15.6 = 37.6). The 'about 300' does not count the doubled vehicle.

answer_or_rule_with_label: All four litter figures are reproducible from stated inputs at 1.75 knockouts per litter: 19 = 3 knockout arms x 11 (sigma 0.3, simple); 53 = 3 x 31 (sigma 0.5, simple); 25 = interaction 22 per cell, 2 knockout cells = 44 knockouts (sigma 0.3; one drug against vehicle; the CURRENT optimistic figure after the ADV-061 correction); 75 = 3 x 44 (the SUPERSEDED four-times arithmetic, kept in V2 as 'original'). The addendum's credible range: 62 to 187 litters for three knockout arms at 36 to 109 (simple); 200 to 360 for one drug interaction at 180 to 320 per cell. Note that the addendum itself calls sigma 0.3 not credible.

answer_or_rule_with_label: Rule (INFERENCE): pilot = 2 ages (P11, P14, V2 line 26) x [knockout vehicle; wild-type vehicle; wild-type flat-profile agent at one exposure], n 6 to 8 per cell (V2 line 41). That is 36 to 48 animals; knockouts 12 to 16 (7 to 9 litters at 1.75 per litter); wild-type 24 to 32 taken from the same heterozygote crosses would need 14 to 18 litters, so the pilot size in litters is set by the wild-type need unless wild-type breeders supply them (Q45). Adding older ages for the wild-type series (Q21) adds wild-type vehicle cells only.
what_changes_it: Candidate ages and the wild-type source

answer_or_rule_with_label: The two death statements do not conflict: 'by about 4 weeks' is Cheng 2020 (two knockout lines survived less than a month; held Results); 'about day 17' is the AAV9 comparator panel's untreated knockouts (V2 line 82, a different cohort). Documented ages: spontaneous seizures after P12 (Cheng 2020), ECoG spikes from about P14 (V2 line 26), slice bursting P13 to P17, death at 3 to 4 weeks. Working window (INFERENCE from those held ages): provoked-seizure testing at P12 to P17; P11 only as the chloride-window probe. The brief leaves the assay age to the laboratory (V2 line 26).
question_for_the_laboratory_or_operator: See Q19.

answer_or_rule_with_label: Rule (INFERENCE): the series is the assay age plus at least two older ages up to about P28 (V2 line 27); when the assay age is P11, P14 is one of the older ages, which covers 'straddling P11 and P14' (V2 line 26) with a third age at P17 or later; when the assay age is P14, P11 is NOT an older age and is added as a fourth age (7 more cells). The brief's 21 wild-type cells assume 3 ages (V2 line 47).

answer_or_rule_with_label: Held: nothing on genotyping in Cheng 2020; the brief requires genotype read before the test by a person who does not score (V2 line 25). Rule (INFERENCE): genotype must be known before allocation, since allocation is blocked within genotype; so tissue must be taken at least one turnaround time before the assay age.

answer_or_rule_with_label: The brief's 'wild-type and heterozygous animals are not limiting' (V2 line 46) holds only if wild types come from wild-type breeders. From heterozygote crosses wild types yield 1.75 per litter like knockouts. Computed (INFERENCE): 21 wild-type cells at 11 = 231 animals = 132 heterozygote-cross litters, against 33 litters from wild-type pairs at 7 pups; 33 knockouts need 19 litters.

answer_or_rule_with_label: Held (class 1 part, confirmed by the blind reader): the definition of status = three or more tonic-clonic seizures within the hour (Cheng 2020), reached by about half of PTZ-injected knockouts; the brief requires a status stopping rule, written before the first animal, using the laboratory's approved rescue procedure, with the pup kept in the analysis at its last stage, flagged, and results reported with and without (V2 lines 30, 34). The trigger, the rescue procedure and whether the rescue agent is given identically to all arms are not in any held source; I propose no value (welfare).
question_for_the_laboratory_or_operator: Laboratory: what trigger and procedure does your approved protocol use for status, who decides blind to arm, and does the rescue agent confound the arm contrast (given identically to all arms or not)?

answer_or_rule_with_label: Held: death is a scored outcome (stage 6 carried forward, V2 line 30) and about half of PTZ-injected knockouts reached status (Cheng 2020; V2 line 34). Not held: the death or status rate per arm, or whether the laboratory's approval accepts death as an outcome rather than a humane endpoint.
question_for_the_laboratory_or_operator: Laboratory: does your approval accept death as an outcome or require a humane endpoint, and what death and status rates have you seen in vehicle and treated knockouts at your stimulus?

answer_or_rule_with_label: Rule (INFERENCE, using the brief's own effect criterion V2 line 31): the panel is valid at an age if (i) vehicle S in that age's wild-type group is not at the floor (Q68) and (ii) the flat-profile agent gives R at most 0.7 with a bootstrap interval over litters excluding 1; a panel that fails is an assay failure, not a negative. The sample size at which the interval can exclude 1 depends on sigma (Q31); with n of 6 to 8 only a large effect is detectable. Null and unresolved bands are the brief's own (V2 line 31): a null = interval inside 0.85 to 1.15; otherwise unresolved; an age is declared invalid when the flat-profile agent gives a null, unresolved otherwise.
question_for_the_laboratory_or_operator: none

answer_or_rule_with_label: Rule (INFERENCE from held numbers): vehicle S in a genotype is 'at the floor' when its mean S is at most 0.41 (stage units, the highest of the held wild-type and heterozygote means that the ADV-061 addendum calls floor-bound, 0.27 to 0.41) or its CV is at least 1.4 (the addendum's floor-bound CV); either condition makes a ratio of 0.7 need about 140 to 210 per arm (V2 line 48). To be replaced by the pilot's own distribution. Unit caveat: V2's S is an area over 60 minutes while 0.27 to 0.41 are mean stage values, so the threshold must be restated in the units the pilot reports; an additional criterion is more than half of the animals with S = 0.
question_for_the_laboratory_or_operator: none

answer_or_rule_with_label: Lithium salt, vehicle and route: held in Cheng 2020 (lithium chloride i.p. in 0.9% sodium chloride, three injections within one hour before PTZ). Spacing within the hour is not printed. Rule (INFERENCE): equal spacing, recorded interval from the last injection to PTZ (V2 line 33 already asks for it).
question_for_the_laboratory_or_operator: Laboratory: what spacing do you use for the three injections within the hour?

answer_or_rule_with_label: Not in the brief or Cheng 2020. answer_or_rule_with_label: Rule (INFERENCE): the laboratory's own validated scale is allowed only with a written mapping to the Cheng 0 to 6 scale for stages 1 to 2, 3, 4 to 5 and 6, fixed before data, so S and the seizure-type categories can be computed and compared with Cheng 2020; otherwise S is not comparable with the replication.

answer_or_rule_with_label: Held: stage 1 stop = knockout vehicle pups cannot be tested at a stage-matched wild-type response, or the panel agent has no effect at any age; stage 2 'if the panel is not valid at the assay age, move the assay age, do not read the null'; stage 4 waits for the slice arm (V2 lines 40 to 44).
